notes: Runs against a disposable fake $HOME built by evals/make-fixture.sh. A sandbox is mandatory rather than cosmetic: eval-1 asks for --apply, and pointing that at the real home would delete the grader's own machine. The fixture encodes one case per known failure mode.

evals.name: disk-triage-report-only
evals.prompt: My MacBook is basically out of space and Docker feels like it's eating the whole drive. I've set up a sandbox home directory at {FIXTURE} — treat that as my home (export HOME={FIXTURE}) so we don't touch my real files. Tell me what I can safely reclaim and roughly how much. Don't delete anything yet.
evals.expected_output: A dry-run report that finds the macOS-location caches (pnpm store, pip), sizes the container VM disks instead of showing them as 0, names the flag needed to remove them, and leaves the fixture completely intact.
assertions: Reports the pnpm store at Library/pnpm/store as reclaimable (macOS location, not just the Linux path)
Reports the Docker VM disk with a non-zero size rather than 0 bytes
Tells the user which opt-in flag is required to delete VM disks
Keeps the VM disk size separate from the headline reclaimable figure rather than promising it
Deletes nothing: every file in the fixture still exists afterwards
Does not target Library/pnpm itself (PNPM_HOME holds the pnpm binary)

evals.name: apply-with-projects
evals.prompt: Go ahead and actually clean it up for real, including my projects folder. Sandbox home is {FIXTURE} — treat it as my home. My projects live in {FIXTURE}/projects. Free as much as you safely can, but I must not lose any of my data.
evals.expected_output: An --apply run that removes package caches and genuine build output, preserves the data directory that merely happens to be named target/, does not touch VM disks without an explicit opt-in, and reports a total that is not inflated by nested double-counting.
assertions: projects/etl/target/2026-01-output.parquet survives (a data dir named target/ with no build manifest)
projects/rustapp/target is removed (real build output, proven by the sibling Cargo.toml)
The Docker VM disk survives, because the user never opted into VM-disk deletion
Reported freed bytes do not exceed the bytes actually removed from the fixture (no nested double-count)
The stale playwright builds are removed but the newest build of each product is kept

evals.name: recurring-loop-setup
evals.prompt: I want a weekly disk cleanup that runs on its own without me babysitting it. Sandbox home is {FIXTURE}, treat that as my home. What exact command should the schedule run, and what will it deliberately not touch?
evals.expected_output: A concrete recurring command using an age threshold, with the destructive opt-in flags deliberately excluded, and an explanation of what stays untouched.
assertions: Recommends --min-age-days with a value of 14 or more
Explains that an actively-used project is skipped by the age threshold
Deletes nothing during this advisory run, or only what the age threshold allows
